findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed handwashing to occur in triple sink. Discussed with PIC, education was provided and hands were rewashed at hand sink. Ensure hand washing is done solely at hand sinks.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(A) Cleaning Procedure. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands or arms for at least 20 seconds, using a cleaning compound in a HANDWASHING SINK that is equipped as specified under § 5-202.12 and Subpart 6-301.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed cooked burgers to be hot holding in crock pot at 125F. Discussed with PIC, crockpot was placed on a warmer setting. Burgers are cooked on grill then moved to crock pot for hot holding. Inspector later observed hot holding tempatures of 145F. Ensure any TCS item being hot held is kept at or above 135F.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: Observed 2 bottles of sanitizer to be resting on the same shelf as TCS food items. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper chemical storage locations and sanitizer bottles were relocated. Ensure all chemicals are stored in a way that prevents any possible contamination.
findings.citation_text: 7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
Observed no allergen training to be present for all CFM’s. Discussed with PIC, CFM’s will complete the required allergen training. Ensure all CFM’s have completed the required allergen training and the correct documention is available during all hours of operation. 


410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed ice machine to have a build up of bacteria/mold to be present. Discussed with PIC, ice machine will be cleaned. Ensure staff is cleaning ice machine at a frequency that prevents build up.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC. 

Observed no signed employee health reporting agreements available for the facility. Facility has misplaced the folder (paperwork was present during last few routine inspections). Provided copy for the facility. Ensure all staff read and sign the document (including bar staff). Ensure new hires read and sign the documents as a part of onboarding. Keep copies of the paperwork in a public health folder or binder. Inspector will follow-up on 4/1/24.

Inspector is leaving SCDPH on 3/29/24. Inspector instructed PIC to text AS photos of the signed employee health reporting agreements next week before 3/29 to put a Spot Check in CDP and close out the violation. Cell: 217-891-3012.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Observed several of the pizza tray’s for the pizza ovens to have food splash and grease on the grates and lips of the tray. Discussed routine cleaning with PIC. Ensure staff is aware to wash, rinse, and sanitize this part of the pizza oven. The base removable catches for the pizza ovens were all very clean. PIC cleaned the trays on site. COS.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-101.19: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. 

Observed all the reach-in freezers to have significant frost. Discussed routine de-frosting of the reach-in freezers with PIC. PIC indicated that the freezers will be each defrosted soon. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

Observed multiple employees to be missing food handler’s licenses in the public health folder. Discussed with PIC. The folder should be cleaned out of old licenses and former employee information. Ensure all staff has a valid food handler’s license (good for 3 years). Ensure copies are left in the facility public health folder. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

Observed food handler to wash hands properly, then turn off the faucet without a barrier to protect against cross contamination. Discussed with employee. Detailed proper hand washing technique (warm water, lather with soap for 20 seconds, rinse, utilize paper towel, turn faucets off with barrier such as the used paper towel). Cross contamination concerns with hand washing. COS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Observed the soda nozzle holder to have pink mold accumulating at the base. Inspector pointed out the mold to the owner/PIC with a flashlight. Discussed routine cleaning of the nozzle holder, as well as the soda nozzle itself. PIC began to wash, rinse, and sanitize the nozzle holder during the inspection. Ensure staff is aware to clean this food-contact piece of equipment. COS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

Observed the bleach spray bottle to have 0 ppm. Sanitizer bottle was re-made with bleach. Facility has test strips to check concentration levels. Discussed with PIC. 50 ppm once remade. COS.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

Observed the allergen training certifications to be expired. Allergen training certifications are valid for 3 years. All certified food protection manager’s (CFPM’s) must have this training certification and keep valid. Discussed with PIC. Provided educational handout on how to obtain the license. Ensure all CFPM’s complete the training and keep copies in the public health binder.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. 

A container of utensils appears to have had BBQ sauce spill at some point into it that is soiling both the bottom of the container and multiple utensils in the container. Inspector discussed with the PIC and the container was moved to dish for cleaning.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Nozzles on the soda gun at the bar are observed not to be clean to sight and touch. Wash, rinse, sanitize routinely. The holes and the rim were cleaned during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

Observed the soda gun to have an accumulation of bacterial growth in the holes that dispense drinks. Discussed with the PIC and instructed to ensure that all food contact surfaces are maintained clean. Just soaking these items over night is not always sufficient to maintain clean.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
750-130 Ready to eat food shall be stored in a matter to prevent cross-contamination.

Observed a cell phone to be sitting on top of single sheets of foil. The foil is used for carry out orders and comes into contact with foods. Discussed other location for the cell phone to be placed in the kitchen (it is used for work purposes) that would not contaminate foods or food contact surfaces. The phone was moved during the inspection.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment:
750-530a Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

Observed a cup in the kitchen area to be without lid. Cups in the food prep areas are allowed only if they have both a lid and a straw. The issue was discussed with the PIC and the cup removed during the inspection.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
750-1210e  Equipment attached to walls and ceilings shall be easily clean able and shall be maintained in good repair.

Observed the vents on the condenser in the walk in cooler to be heavily soiled with dust. Instructed the PIC to clean often enough so as to prevent accumulation.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

Observed the soda gun nozzle to be contaminated with bacterial growth in the holes and mold build up around the inner sides of both the nozzle and the mechanism. Instructed employees to clean often enough to prevent build up of soilage.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment:
750-860 The food-contact surfaces of fixed equipment shall also be  protected from contamination.

Observed the bottom of the holder of the soda gun holder to be soiled with bacterial growth. Instructed PIC to clean regularly enough to prevent accumulation.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
750-880 Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user.

Observed straws on the bar to not be protected from outside contamination. Straws should be pre-packaged or stored in some fashion to prevent contamination from sneezing, coughing, unintentional hand contact, ect. Discussed with the PIC and instructed to remedy by the next inspection.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment: 750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination. Observed bacterial slime in the nozzle spouts of the soda gun. Made the manager aware of the issue and suggested cleaning practices to better prevent the accumulation and produce a more sanitary situation.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750-800 Observed a small accumulation of mold beginning to develop in the ice machine. Ice from this machine is used for drinks in the facility and poses a potential for cross-contamination into a clients drink. Was told that the machine had been cleaned recently. Suggested to management to clean more often.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: 750-1210e  Equipment attached to walls and ceilings shall be easily clean able and shall be maintained in good repair. Observed an accumulation of dust on the vents of air ducts in the kitchen. Suggested cleaning them on a regular basis.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Observed the wall next to the fryer to have some spillage. Clean the wall.
750-1220 Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed all reach in freezers to have some frost accumulation.  Defrost all the freezers to make them smooth and easily cleanable.
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Wholesome, sound condition
findings.comment:
Observed four dented cans at the facility.  Two cans of mushrooms and two cans of tomato sauce were pulled during the inspection and should be returned.
750-100 Food shall be in sound condition, free from spoilage, filth, and other contamination and shall be safe for human consumption.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment: Observed no QUAT test kit in the facility.  Provide a QUAT test kit to check the proper sanitizer concentration.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
Observed wet wiping cloths stored on the bar.  Wiping cloths should be stored in a sanitizer concentration.
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
1) Observed the fryer handle on door to be soiled. 2) Observed area holding fry basket to have a heavy grease buildup. Degrease the area. 3) Observed the tray of the pizza oven to be soiled (bottom oven)  Clean the non food contact surfaces.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed a container holding utensils to have small debris buildup in the bottom of container.  Clean the non food contact surface.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
Observed no lid on the trash can in the men's restroom.  Replace the lid.
750-1110d Toilet facilities shall be kept clean and in good repair and free of objectionable odors. A supply of toilet tissue shall be provided at each toilet at all times. Easily cleanable, covered receptacles shall be provided for waste materials.

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.comment:
Observed the back door to have a small gap at the bottom of the door.  Replace the strip so no daylight is seen.  Follow up will be performed.
750-1170 Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Observed an absence of caulk at the handwashing sink in the kitchen.  Owner stated that a new handsink was put in place of an old one.  Caulk the handsink to the wall.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.
